record.original_question: Find an efficient decoding algorithm for an infinite family of self-dual codes, or ideally for all self-dual codes.

evidence.quote: Open Question 10.1. Find an efficient decoding algorithm for a family of self-dual codes or for all self-dual codes.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field and let $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ be a linear code of length $n$ and dimension $k$. The dual code is $C^\perp = \{ x \in \mathbb{F}_q^n : \langle x, c \rangle = 0 \text{ for all } c \in C \}$, where $\langle x, c \rangle = \sum_{i=1}^n x_i c_i$. The code $C$ is called self-dual if $C = C^\perp$ (which forces $n = 2k$). Given a received word $y = c + e \in \mathbb{F}_q^n$, where $c \in C$ and $e$ is an error vector of Hamming weight at most $\lfloor (d-1)/2 \rfloor$ (with $d$ the minimum distance of $C$), the decoding problem asks to recover $c$ from $y$.

Exhibit an infinite family $\{C_n\}$ of self-dual codes (with $n \to \infty$) together with a decoding algorithm running in time polynomial in $n$ that corrects up to $\lfloor (d_n-1)/2 \rfloor$ errors for every $C_n$ in the family. More ambitiously, produce such a polynomial-time decoding algorithm that works for all self-dual codes (given a generator matrix as input).
artifact.status_search_result: No general efficient decoding algorithm for self-dual codes is known. Efficient decoders exist only for sporadic specific codes (e.g., the binary Golay [24,12,8], several Type II [32,16,8] codes, the [48,24,12] code, and certain extremal [40,20,8] codes) or for restricted classes such as self-dual codes admitting an automorphism of odd order. The general problem, posed by Huffman–Pless and reiterated as Open Question 10.1 in the cited problem list, remains open.

status_evidence.title: On decoding of a specific type of self-dual codes
status_evidence.snippet: Efficient decoding algorithms exist only for specific self-dual codes such as the binary Golay code and a few Type II codes; no general method is known.
status_evidence.claim: No general efficient decoder for self-dual codes is known; only sporadic specific codes have efficient decoders.

status_evidence.title: A Projection Decoding of a Binary Extremal Self-Dual Code of Length 40
status_evidence.snippet: New efficient decoding algorithms are developed for an extremal binary doubly-even self-dual [40,20,8] code via projection.
status_evidence.claim: Recent works develop decoders only for specific extremal self-dual codes, indicating the general problem remains open.
